rows.rationale: Upstream d64e35a fixes the coreutils-9.5 mcel_scan pointer-advance implementation. Actual old 8.32-41 source plus every vendor patch touching uniq were independently inspected: only i18n patch applies, it advances a bounded pos for skips and leaves -w in length-clipped different/memcmp; no defective mcel_scan/ep-length expansion implementation. Old i18n differs overall from newer 43 but exact src/uniq.c patch body is independently equal. Actual coreutils ELF/dispatch hashes match original x86_64 RPM.
rows.source_architecture_boundary: Signed source RPM query reports aarch64. Its NEVR/source archive and generic uniq vendor source match the actual x86_64 installed package SOURCERPM name, with no architecture condition on this patch; this is source-scope corroboration, not a cryptographic reproducible-build claim that this particular SRPM blob produced the old x86_64 binary.

rows.rationale: Official fault is the BIG5-HKSCS gconv implementation. Exact old 2.34-283 SRPM source maps it to BIG5HKSCS.so in gconv-modules-extra.conf. Complete actual payload contains only seven named other gconv ELF modules; BIG5HKSCS implementation and extra configuration are absent. Exact old source also includes the c580 pending-character state reset, but this record does not infer every binary is fixed from version alone.

Official advisory confines the faulty strncasecmp implementation to Power8. All 70 actual runtime ELF headers are ELF64 little-endian e_machine=62 (x86_64), including original RPM libc. Actual libc defines x86 SSE/AVX/EVEX strncasecmp implementations. No claim that Power8 implementation is fixed.

Official affected component is libstdc++ file-stream buffering, structurally separate from libgcc. Exact actual libgcc_s original RPM hash, complete package file map and all-runtime dependency inventory contain no libstdc++ library/tool or streambuf implementation symbols; libgcc_s DT_NEEDED is libc.so.6 only. GCC source libgcc build/files and libstdc++ fstream.tcc corroborate the component separation. No claim libstdc++ itself is fixed or that all components of gcc SRPM are safe.

Official affected implementation is libiberty/rust-demangle.c, not libgcc runtime unwinding. Actual RPM database maps libgcc to one original-hash libgcc_s ELF plus links/build-id/licenses; no libiberty or demangler tool/library is present. All actual ELF defined/undefined symbols and DT_NEEDED were inspected, without Rust demangle implementation symbols or libiberty dependency. Official Red Hat 2022-27943 statement explicitly excludes libgcc; GCC source/spec additionally separates libgcc from libiberty. This is package-component scope, not proof all GCC-source components are fixed.

Actual ncurses-base package is terminfo data, directories and license, with no executable implementation. Source defect is parser handling of source terminfo strings, not a defect located in this binary data subpackage. IMPORTANT: same image DOES include affected implementation via ncurses-libs/libtic; this per-package mapping never clears that other tuple or the image as a whole.

Actual ncurses-libs contains original RPM libtic.so.6.2, SHA169fd0998038aa0987f25827f8ce0fe9ee9ea82846958237c22f57bf0137209f, defining _nc_wrap_entry/_nc_parse_entry/_nc_read_entry_source. Accurate old source parse_entry.c L172 and L353 lacks the two upstream 20230424 _nc_save_str NULL checks. Absence of tic executable or external ELF imports does not prove safety. Red Hat statement about libncurses is insufficient for present libtic.
rows.next_evidence: Verify fully prepared exact old source and real libtic implementation; apply actual official fix and prove new binary/source/test identity, or retain blocker. Do not classify as component absent.
